questions.question: On modern models with built-in (adaptive) thinking, when is asking for visible reasoning still most useful?
options: Never, since internal thinking makes it pointless
On every request, to maximise accuracy
When you or a reviewer need to inspect or audit how the answer was reached
questions.explanation: Built-in thinking handles quality; visible reasoning is valuable when you need transparency, auditing or prompt debugging.

questions.question: Which task is least likely to benefit from step-by-step reasoning?
options: Calculating a pro-rated bonus across months
Checking a claim against several policy rules
Comparing three vendor proposals to recommend one
questions.explanation: Simple lookups do not need intermediate steps, so reasoning only adds tokens and latency.

questions.question: Why separate reasoning into `<working>` tags and the result into `<answer>` tags?
options: It makes the model reason more deeply
Readers and code can find and extract the final result easily
It is required for chain-of-thought to work
It hides the reasoning from the model itself
questions.explanation: Keeping reasoning and answer apart makes the output easy to scan and parse.

questions.question: Which self-check instruction is most effective?
options: MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO MISTAKES
Verify that every figure comes from the <report> tags and that the percentages add up to 100
questions.explanation: Self-checks work best with concrete, checkable criteria rather than vague or shouted reminders.
